title: 「The moment _ the minute」表示「一……便……」
titleEn: Using the moment / the minute to show immediate sequence

source.file: Sentence Structure 118 -「The moment _ the minute」表示「一……便……」.pdf
omissions: English versions of Chinese-only Important Rules and Benefits headings are faithful editorial translations.

formula: The moment / The minute + subject + verb, subject + verb + other information

formulas.formula: The moment / The minute + subject + verb, subject + verb + other information
Subject + verb + the moment / the minute + subject + verb

example: The moment I saw the bus, I started running.
exampleZh: 我一看見巴士，便開始跑。

examples.en: The moment I saw the bus, I started running.
examples.zh: 我一看見巴士，便開始跑。
examples.highlight: The moment I saw the bus

examples.en: I started running the minute I saw the bus.
examples.zh: 我一看見巴士，便開始跑。
examples.highlight: the minute I saw the bus

rules.zh: 表示第二件事立即發生 The moment 和 the minute 都表示一件事發生後，另一件事幾乎立即發生，相當於： ● 一……便…… ● 一……就……
rules.en: Use the structure when the second event happens almost immediately after the first. Both the moment and the minute mean ‘as soon as’ or ‘immediately when’.
examples: as soon as
immediately when
The moment the door opened, the dog ran outside.

rules.zh: The minute 並非指真正的一分鐘 在這個句型中，the minute 不表示「六十秒」，而是表示「就在……發生時」。
rules.en: The minute in this structure does not mean a literal sixty seconds; it means ‘at the very time that something happens’.
examples: I called her the minute I heard the news.

rules.zh: 兩個說法意思非常接近 The moment 和 the minute 在這個用法中意思幾乎相同。 ● the moment：適合日常說話及一般寫作。 ● the minute：語氣通常稍為口語化，但仍可用於一般寫作。
rules.en: The moment and the minute have almost the same meaning here. The moment suits everyday speech and general writing, while the minute is usually a little more conversational but can still be used in general writing.
examples: the moment：適合日常說話及一般寫作。
the minute：語氣通常稍為口語化，但仍可用於一般寫作。

rules.zh: 句型放在句首時要加逗號 句型放在主句後面時，通常不需要逗號。
rules.en: Use a comma when the time expression comes first; when it follows the main clause, a comma is not normally needed.

rules.zh: 談及未來時，時間子句不用 will 即使整句談及未來，the moment / the minute 後面通常使用現在式。 與其他句型的分別 The moment / the minute 與 By the time The moment / the minute 強調第二件事立即發生。 By the time 表示在某個時間點之前，另一件事已經發生或完成，不一定是立即發生。 重點分別： ● the moment / the minute：一件事發生後，另一件事立即發生。 ● by the time：到某個時間點時，另一件事已經發生或完成。 The moment / the minute 與 Once Once 通常強調某件事完成或某個條件成立後，另一件事便可以發生。 The moment / the minute 則特別強調兩件事之間幾乎沒有時間間隔。 The moment / the minute 與 When When 只表示兩件事在某個時間發生，未必表示第二件事立即發生。 The moment / the minute 明確表示第二件事緊接第一件事發生。 The moment / the minute 與 If If 表示條件，事情可能發生，也可能不發生。 The moment / the minute 表示時間關係，重點是事情發生時，另一件事會立即跟着發生。
rules.en: For future meaning, do not use will in the time clause; use a present form after the moment or the minute. Distinguish this structure from related linkers: the moment or the minute emphasizes that the second event follows immediately, whereas by the time says that something has already happened or been completed before a reference point and need not be immediate. Once emphasizes that an event is complete or a condition is met before another event becomes possible, but the moment or the minute specifically stresses an almost nonexistent time gap. When identifies a time without necessarily implying an immediate second event. If introduces a condition that may or may not occur, while the moment or the minute expresses a time relationship and what follows immediately when the event occurs.
examples: I will call you the moment I arrive.
the moment / the minute：一件事發生後，另一件事立即發生。
by the time：到某個時間點時，另一件事已經發生或完成。
The moment I got home, I called my mother.
By the time I got home, everyone had already gone to bed.
Once you understand the pattern, it becomes easier.
The moment you understand the pattern, you will notice the difference.
When pressure rises, good leaders speak more carefully.
The moment pressure rose, the leader called an emergency meeting.
If you ignore early warnings, small problems become expensive mistakes.
The moment you notice an early warning, report it.

benefits.zh: 清楚表示「立即發生」 這個句型能讓讀者立即明白，第二件事並不是很久之後才發生，而是緊接第一件事發生。 第二句更清楚地表達學生立即離開。
benefits.en: It clearly expresses that something happens immediately. Readers understand that the second event does not occur much later but follows directly after the first; in the comparison, the second sentence makes the students’ immediate departure clearer.
examples: When the bell rang, the students left.
The moment the bell rang, the students left.

benefits.zh: 令故事和描述更有畫面 這個句型特別適合敘述突發事件、反應或故事情節，讓讀者感受到事情迅速發生。
benefits.en: It makes stories and descriptions more vivid. The structure is especially effective for sudden events, reactions and plot developments because it lets readers feel how quickly events unfold.
examples: The moment she opened the box, everyone became silent.

benefits.zh: 把兩件相關事件連接起來 你可以把兩個短句合併成一個完整句子，清楚顯示兩件事的時間關係。
benefits.en: It connects two related events. You can combine two short sentences into one complete sentence and show their time relationship clearly.
examples: The minute the rain stopped, we went outside.

benefits.zh: 避免重複使用 when 或 as soon as 這個句型提供另一種自然說法，令寫作和說話不會反覆使用相同的連接詞。
benefits.en: It avoids repeatedly using when or as soon as by providing another natural expression and adding variety to speech and writing.

benefits.zh: 提供容易使用的說話框架 你可以先記住以下框架，再加入自己的內容：
benefits.en: It provides an easy speaking frame: learn the pattern first, then insert your own content.
examples: The moment I heard the news, I called my friend.
